newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico brings fiscal charges against prominent critic.
newsitem.headline: Mexico brings fiscal charges against prominent critic.

text.p: Mexican authorities said late Thursday they were seeking the arrest of the director of El Universal, once a staunchly pro-government newspaper that has taken a highly critical line against the government.

The Attorney General's Office, acting on a complaint from the Finance Ministry, also said it was bringing charges of tax evasion against the jailed brother of disgraced former President Carlos Salinas de Gortari.
A government press release said an arrest warrant had been issued against Juan Francisco Ealy Ortiz, director general of El Universal, one of Mexico City's more important newspapers.
Dozens of police surrounded the newspaper building and Ealy Ortiz's home late Thursday, witnesses said.
Authorities said Ealy Ortiz defrauded the government of some $3.7 million in taxes the newspaper owed from fiscal year 1995 and $1.7 million in personal taxes from 1994 and 1995.
Ealy Ortiz's backers immediately alleged that the charges were politically motivated by El Universal's editorial position critical of the government.

"The actions against Early Ortiz speak of an aggression against the independent line of the newspaper," political columnist Carlos Ramirez told Reuters. "For six months we have received threats that the president (Ernesto Zedillo) was upset."

El Universal recently has hired agressive and critical investigative reporters and also runs the column of Jorge Castaneda, one of Mexico's foremost commentators who is often critical of the government.

In the other case, officials said Raul Salinas de Gortari, currently in jail pending charges he masterminded a political murder, owes at least $662,500 in taxes from fiscal year 1992, when he was on the governm+ent payroll as a high-level bureaucrat during his brother's presidency..
"Nonetheless, this tax evasion could turn out to be greater as the fiscal authority is waiting for additional information that has been requested," the Attorney General's Office said.

Since Salinas was jailed last year, forcing his brother to flee the country in exile, various confirmed and unconfirmed reports have surfaced that he stashed up to hundreds of millions of dollars in European bank accounts.
